A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe Testing Most Influential Sets. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks establish matching scientific content, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A1–A4.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulations and empirical analyses across economics, sparrow morphology, and four machine-learning datasets in Section 4 and Appendix A4.

after.justification: v4 retains those original simulation and data-analysis results in Section 4 and Appendix A4, including convergence estimates and tests for excessive influence.

M1.justification: The exact least-squares influence formula, EVD selection, block-maxima estimation, adaptive greedy approximation, and hypothesis-testing procedure in Section 3 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Normal/t(5) simulation scenarios, economic-development and sparrow datasets, and Law School, Adult Income, Boston Housing, and Communities & Crime applications.

E2.justification: The corrected and uncorrected Gumbel/block-maxima comparisons in Figures 2 and A1 are unchanged. No evaluated comparison method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains identical simulation sample sizes, application sample and subset sizes, regression targets, and testing procedures. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The convergence analysis in Figure 3 and Table A1, estimation-bias analysis in Figure A1, and influential-set case studies in Section 4.2 and Table A2 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report 1,000 simulation repetitions, mean and ±1 SD displays in Figure 3, and standard deviations and quantiles in Table A1. Standard-error and p-value reporting also match.

E6.justification: All reported values and plotted findings match, including Tables 1, A1, and A2. For example, the Seychelles–Lesotho p-value remains 0.216 and the full-set Communities & Crime p-value remains 0.4914.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Proposition 1, Theorems 1–2, corollaries, and mathematical derivations and proofs in Appendices A1–A3 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about exact influence, extreme-value distributions, principled testing, and empirical applicability.

C2.justification: The empirical interpretations and Section 5 discussion are identical, including qualifications about linear models, independence assumptions, finite-sample EVD estimation, and approximating maximum influence.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 implementation details and the reproducibility statement are unchanged. Both PDFs provide the same code link and dataset-source information.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference entries, and positioning relative to influence functions, subset-selection methods, and extreme-value theory are identical.

P1.justification: v4 adds the running text Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All body prose, headings, and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The publication header appears above the existing top rule on every page, and the first-page arXiv stamp changes. Rendered page bodies, including all figures, tables, equations, and their placement, are otherwise pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: v4 changes only publication and version markings. The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
